topic.title: No-Regret Learning and Equilibrium in Multiagent Games
topic.overview: When several agents learn simultaneously, each agent changes the environment faced by the others. This topic studies regret, convergence, and equilibrium in repeated and Markov games. Low regret and stable behavior are distinct goals, and guarantees depend on the game structure and on which learning procedures the other agents follow.
topic.whyItMatters: An algorithm can perform well on average while its current policy keeps oscillating. Last-iterate convergence matters when the final deployed strategy must be useful, while robustness to changing opponents requires different analysis. Equilibrium type also matters: correlated and Nash solutions make different demands.
topic.evolution: A 2004 approach combines no-regret guarantees with convergence analysis in limited settings. Later work sharpens last-iterate results and studies time-varying games. A 2023 method obtains swap-regret guarantees when all agents use its procedure in general-sum Markov games; 2026 offline zero-sum work uses KL regularization under explicit coverage and reference-policy conditions.
openQuestions: When can decentralized learners achieve both low regret and stable final policies?
How do offline coverage assumptions constrain the equilibria that can be learned?

papers.tldr: Weighting reward predictions more heavily than the feedback delay restores stated regret and convergence guarantees for optimistic learning in specified game classes.

papers.title: Near-Optimal Regret-Queue Length Tradeoff in Online Learning for Two-Sided Markets
papers.tldr: The paper develops online pricing with a provably near-optimal trade-off between profit regret and queue lengths in two-sided markets.

papers.title: Optimism Without Regularization: Constant Regret in Zero-Sum Games
papers.tldr: Optimistic Fictitious Play achieves constant regret in two-strategy zero-sum games without regularization, regardless of its tiebreaking rule.

papers.title: Uncoupled and Convergent Learning in Monotone Games under Bandit Feedback
papers.tldr: A mirror-descent algorithm achieves no regret and last-iterate convergence in monotone games with bandit feedback and strongly uncoupled learning.

papers.title: \(\varepsilon\)-Optimally Solving Two-Player Zero-Sum POSGs
papers.tldr: A lossless game reduction enables dynamic-programming methods to compute empirically epsilon-optimal strategies in partially observable zero-sum games.

papers.title: A Direct Second-Order Method for Solving Two-Player Zero-Sum Games
papers.tldr: A hybrid game solver combines global first-order progress with locally superlinear Newton steps, producing order-of-magnitude speedups for high-precision matrix-game solutions.

papers.title: Achieving Logarithmic Regret in KL-Regularized Zero-Sum Markov Games
papers.tldr: New algorithms achieve logarithmic regret in KL-regularized zero-sum games, with bounds that depend inversely on regularization strength.

papers.title: Asymmetric Perturbation in Solving Bilinear Saddle-Point Optimization
papers.tldr: Perturbing only one player’s payoff enables fast equilibrium learning while preserving a solution of the original game.

papers.title: (Doubly) Exponential Lower Bounds for Follow the Regularized Leader in Potential Games
papers.tldr: FTRL can converge exponentially slowly in two-player potential games, while fictitious play can require doubly exponential time with multiple players.

papers.title: Learning in Bayesian Stackelberg Games With Unknown Follower’s Types
papers.tldr: With unknown follower payoffs, no-regret Stackelberg learning is impossible from action feedback alone but achievable with revealed types.

papers.title: Learning in Structured Stackelberg Games
papers.tldr: New complexity measures characterize how leaders can learn effective policies when context predicts an unknown follower type in structured Stackelberg games.

papers.title: Offline Two-Player Zero-Sum Markov Games with KL Regularization
papers.tldr: Under stated coverage and regularization conditions, KL regularization enables fast equilibrium learning in offline zero-sum Markov games.

papers.title: Stronger Benchmarks for Prediction as a Service with Constraints
papers.tldr: A shared prediction algorithm gives multiple constrained decision makers simultaneous dynamic-regret guarantees, even when they react without maintaining state.

papers.title: What Preferences Can—and Cannot—Predict in Multi-Agent Online Learning
papers.tldr: Preference graphs characterize learning stability in subgames, but more general stability requires additional payoff information.
